drawer-dividers.title: Cardboard drawer dividers
drawer-dividers.description: Give socks, stationery and little essentials a place of their own.

requirements.label: Two large corrugated cardboard sheets
requirements.why: Each sheet must span the inside of your drawer.

requirements.label: Scissors
requirements.why: Choose scissors that can safely cut this material.

requirements.label: The drawer to organize
requirements.why: Measure and test the dividers in the actual drawer.

steps.title: Measure the drawer
steps.text: Empty the drawer. Measure its inside width, depth and height. Plan four compartments.
steps.check: Allow 3–5 mm of clearance at the ends.

steps.title: Cut two dividers
steps.text: Cut one strip for the width and one for the depth. Make both about 1 cm lower than the drawer.
steps.check: Dry-fit each strip without forcing it.
steps.safety: Ask an adult to help with thick material. Cut away from your hands and keep small scraps away from young children.

steps.title: Slot the pieces together
steps.text: At each midpoint cut a slot halfway through the height, as wide as the cardboard thickness. Slide the two slots together into a cross.
steps.check: The four compartments stand upright with a snug joint.

steps.title: Fill and test
steps.text: Tape exposed edges, fit the dividers and add light items. Open and close the drawer slowly five times.
steps.check: Nothing catches on the runners or prevents closing.

drawer-dividers.limitations: Use for dry, light items. Keep away from heat; this is not a load-bearing structure.

test.name: Observation
test.instruction: Record the drawer dimensions and successful opening/closing trials.

desk-caddy.title: Cardboard desk caddy
desk-caddy.description: Turn saved cardboard tubes into a tidy home for pens and pencils.

requirements.label: Three clean cardboard tubes
requirements.why: Choose tubes wide enough for stationery.

requirements.label: Cardboard base, about 20 × 15 cm
requirements.why: The base should extend beyond the tubes.

requirements.label: Scissors
requirements.why: Choose scissors that can safely cut this material.

steps.title: Arrange the tubes
steps.text: Arrange three tubes on the base with at least 2 cm around the outside. Mark their positions.
steps.check: The caddy fits well away from the desk edge.

steps.title: Make fixing tabs
steps.text: Cut 1 cm tabs around the bottom of each tube and fold them outward.
steps.check: The tabs lie flat on the base.
steps.safety: Ask an adult to help with thick material. Cut away from your hands and keep small scraps away from young children.

steps.title: Tape to the base
steps.text: Tape every tab to the base, then tape adjacent tubes together.
steps.check: The base stays attached when gently lifted.

steps.title: Load gradually
steps.text: Add pens and pencils one at a time. Practise taking them out and replacing them.
steps.check: It stays upright when using an outside tube.

desk-caddy.limitations: For light stationery. Do not store sharp scissors or hot objects.

test.name: Observation
test.instruction: Record how many pens fit while the base remains level.

cable-rolls.title: Cable storage sleeves
cable-rolls.description: Keep unplugged charging and data cables neatly separated.

requirements.label: Three disconnected USB cables
requirements.why: Intact cables for storage only. Never power them while coiled inside a sleeve.

steps.title: Choose intact cables
steps.text: Disconnect every cable from power and devices. Reject cracked, frayed or scorched cables.
steps.check: Only store cables that are fully disconnected.

steps.title: Coil loosely
steps.text: Coil along the cable’s natural curve. Keep bends gentle near connectors. Choose a tube that does not squeeze the cable.
steps.check: There are no sharp bends.

steps.title: Label and sort
steps.text: Write the cable type on its sleeve. Put one cable in each sleeve and arrange them in the box.
steps.check: Each label is visible and each cable can be removed separately.

cable-rolls.limitations: Never enclose operating cables or power adapters. Tape does not make damaged electrical insulation safe.

test.name: Observation
test.instruction: Try finding a requested cable five times and record successful selections.

jar-storage.title: Labelled storage jars
jar-storage.description: Make small household essentials easy to find in reused food jars.

requirements.label: Two intact glass jars
requirements.why: Wash and fully dry before use.

requirements.label: Scissors
requirements.why: Choose scissors that can safely cut this material.

steps.title: Inspect and dry
steps.text: Use clean, completely dry food jars. Inspect their rims and bases.
steps.check: No cracks or chips.
steps.safety: Reject damaged glass and chemical containers.

steps.title: Sort by use
steps.text: Put one type of item in each jar, such as clips or buttons. Keep sharp objects out.
steps.check: Contents are easy to reach.

steps.title: Label and place
steps.text: Cut and write labels, tape them to the front, and place the jars on a low, stable shelf.
steps.check: Do not stack jars or place them at an edge.

jar-storage.limitations: For household storage, not food preservation or young children’s play.

test.name: Observation
test.instruction: Ask someone to find an item using the labels and record the result.

phone-stand.title: Cardboard phone stand
phone-stand.description: Keep a phone upright for recipes, lessons or a video call.

requirements.label: Two A4-size corrugated cardboard sheets
requirements.why: Makes two side supports and joining strips.

requirements.label: Scissors
requirements.why: Choose scissors that can safely cut this material.

requirements.label: The phone you want to support
requirements.why: Check its size and weight while holding it during the stability test.

steps.title: Mark matching side supports
steps.text: Draw two right triangles with 14 cm bases and 10 cm heights. Extend each base 2 cm at the front to form a support ledge.
steps.check: The supports match.

steps.title: Cut and add stops
steps.text: Cut the supports. Fold small card strips into 1 cm-high stops and tape them to the front ledges.
steps.check: The stops support the phone without covering much of the screen.
steps.safety: Ask an adult to help with thick material. Cut away from your hands and keep small scraps away from young children.

steps.title: Join the supports
steps.text: Space the supports about 7 cm apart. Tape cardboard crosspieces across the back and bottom, securing both sides.
steps.check: The base stays square and both slopes align.

steps.title: Test close to the floor
steps.text: Use a low surface. Hold the phone while gradually transferring its weight. Reinforce the base if it bends or slips.
steps.check: It stays stable with gentle screen taps.

phone-stand.limitations: For light phones, not tablets. Keep away from water and heat.

test.name: Observation
test.instruction: Record base dimensions and five gentle screen-tap trials.

cleaning-cloths.title: Reusable cleaning cloths
cleaning-cloths.description: Give a worn T-shirt a second life as washable cleaning cloths.

requirements.label: One clean knitted T-shirt
requirements.why: Soft cotton or knit fabric without hard decorations.

requirements.label: Scissors
requirements.why: Choose scissors that can safely cut this material.

steps.title: Choose clean fabric
steps.text: Wash and dry the shirt. Choose areas without zips, buttons or stiff prints.
steps.check: No mould or hazardous contamination.

steps.title: Mark squares
steps.text: Mark approximately 20 × 20 cm squares on the body of the shirt, avoiding thick seams.
steps.check: A folded square fits comfortably in your hand.

steps.title: Cut and spot-test
steps.text: Cut the squares, remove loose threads, and test on a small hidden area first.
steps.check: No scratching or colour transfer.
steps.safety: Ask an adult to help with thick material. Cut away from your hands and keep small scraps away from young children.

steps.title: Separate and wash
steps.text: Keep separate cloths for different areas. Wash after use and dry completely before storing.
steps.check: Bathroom cloths stay separate from food-preparation surfaces.

cleaning-cloths.limitations: For ordinary dust and spills, not disinfection. Never mix cleaning products.

test.name: Observation
test.instruction: Compare dry and damp cloths on similar marks and record observations.

sock-duster.title: Sock dusting mitt
sock-duster.description: Put an odd sock to work on shelves and furniture edges.

requirements.label: One soft clean sock
requirements.why: Must fit comfortably over your hand.

steps.title: Inspect the sock
steps.text: Choose a clean, dry sock without grit or hard decorations.
steps.check: Seams will not scratch the surface.

steps.title: Wear and spot-test
steps.text: Pull the sock over your hand. Lightly wipe a small hidden area first.
steps.check: The surface stays unscratched and unchanged.

steps.title: Dust from top to bottom
steps.text: Wipe reachable shelves from top to bottom. Turn to a clean area as dust builds up, then wash and dry the sock.
steps.check: Keep dust away from your face and wash your hands afterwards.

sock-duster.limitations: Avoid operating appliances, heat, mould and hazardous dust. Do not climb a chair to reach higher.

test.name: Observation
test.instruction: Record tested surfaces and any marks or shed fibres.

lint-roller.title: Quick tape lint roller
lint-roller.description: Lift loose hair and lint with a cardboard tube and tape.

requirements.label: Scissors
requirements.why: Choose scissors that can safely cut this material.

steps.title: Choose suitable tape
steps.text: Use low-tack removable tape. Avoid strong adhesive tape.
steps.check: Spot-test the tape on hidden fabric first.

steps.title: Wrap sticky side out
steps.text: Wrap tape around the middle of the tube with adhesive facing outward. Overlap the ends and leave the tube ends free to hold.
steps.check: The tape stays wrapped as the tube turns.

steps.title: Roll gently and discard tape
steps.text: Roll lightly on the tested fabric. Replace loaded tape and put used tape in general waste.
steps.check: No adhesive residue or pulled fabric fibres.

lint-roller.limitations: Not for silk, leather, delicate fabrics, pets or skin. This method still consumes disposable tape.

test.name: Observation
test.instruction: Record lint pickup and any residue on the test fabric.

sew-button.title: Sew a loose button back on
sew-button.description: Repair a loose flat button with a needle and thread.

requirements.label: One flat two- or four-hole button
Sewing needle
requirements.why: Must fit through the button holes.

requirements.label: Fabric or garment to repair
requirements.why: The attachment area must be intact.

requirements.label: Scissors
requirements.why: Choose scissors that can safely cut this material.

steps.title: Position and thread
steps.text: Align the button with its buttonhole. Thread the needle and knot the thread end.
steps.check: The original spot is not torn or weakened.
steps.safety: Keep needles and buttons away from young children. Account for the needle before and after sewing.

steps.title: Sew through the holes
steps.text: Pass the needle from the back of the fabric through one hole, then down through its neighbour. Repeat about 5–6 times; sew the second pair for a four-hole button.
steps.check: Leave a small gap under the button for the buttonhole fabric.

steps.title: Secure the back
steps.text: Bring the needle to the back. Slip under an existing stitch to form a loop, pass through the loop and tighten. Repeat before trimming.
steps.check: The knot holds under a gentle pull.

steps.title: Test fastening
steps.text: Fasten and unfasten five times, then store the needle safely.
steps.check: The button stays attached without pulling the fabric.

sew-button.limitations: For ordinary clothing, not safety equipment. Repair torn attachment fabric first.

test.name: Observation
test.instruction: Record five fastening/unfastening trials.

fabric-patch.title: Patch a small fabric tear
fabric-patch.description: Mend a small tear in a fabric bag or garment with a simple sewn patch.

requirements.label: Damaged fabric and a patch scrap
requirements.why: The patch must extend at least 2 cm beyond every side of the tear.

requirements.label: Sewing needle
requirements.why: Use a needle that passes through the fabric without force.

requirements.label: Sewing thread
requirements.why: Enough to stitch around the patch.

requirements.label: Scissors
requirements.why: Choose scissors that can safely cut this material.

steps.title: Measure the tear
steps.text: Lay the fabric flat. Measure the tear and cut a patch extending at least 2 cm on every side.
steps.check: The fabric around the tear is sound.

steps.title: Turn under the edges
steps.text: Turn the patch edges under by about 5 mm and lay it smoothly over the tear.
steps.check: Raw edges are tucked under.

steps.title: Stitch all the way around
steps.text: Thread and knot the needle. Sew small, even running stitches through both layers about 3 mm from the folded edge. Knot securely at the back.
steps.check: All sides are attached and the needle is accounted for.
steps.safety: Children need supervision with needles. Do not use rusty needles.

steps.title: Check the repair
steps.text: Gently pull around the patch. Restitch any edge that opens.
steps.check: No open edge or puckering.

fabric-patch.limitations: Not for load-bearing straps, protective equipment or large tears.

test.name: Observation
test.instruction: Record tear size and inspect the stitches after light use.

zipper-pull.title: Replace a missing zipper pull
zipper-pull.description: Add an easy-grip pull when the zipper slider still works.

requirements.label: Thin cord about 15 cm long
requirements.why: Must fit through the slider’s pull hole.

requirements.label: Scissors
requirements.why: Choose scissors that can safely cut this material.

requirements.label: A bag or garment missing only its zipper pull
requirements.why: The slider and teeth must be intact.

steps.title: Check the slider
steps.text: Use a zipper with intact teeth, a working slider and an intact pull attachment hole.
steps.check: Only the pull is missing.

steps.title: Thread a loop
steps.text: Fold the cord in half. Pass the fold through the slider hole, then pass both loose ends through the loop.
steps.check: The cord stays clear of the zipper teeth.

steps.title: Tie and trim
steps.text: Snug the loop, tie the loose ends together, and slowly open and close five times. Trim excess ends.
steps.check: The knot holds and the zipper runs freely.

zipper-pull.limitations: For ordinary bags. This does not repair damaged teeth or sliders and is not for safety equipment.

test.name: Observation
test.instruction: Count successful opening/closing trials without the cord loosening.

tshirt-tote.title: No-sew T-shirt tote
tshirt-tote.description: Make a light-duty reusable bag from an unworn T-shirt.

requirements.label: Scissors
requirements.why: Choose scissors that can safely cut this material.

steps.title: Shape the handles
steps.text: Lay the shirt flat. Remove the sleeves along their seams. Widen the neck into a U, leaving shoulder handles at least 5 cm wide.
steps.check: Both handles remain wide and intact.
steps.safety: Ask an adult to help with thick material. Cut away from your hands and keep small scraps away from young children.

steps.title: Cut the fringe
steps.text: Turn inside out and remove the bottom hem. Cut matching 2 cm-wide, 8 cm-long fringes through both layers along the bottom.
steps.check: Front and back fringes line up.

steps.title: Tie the bottom closed
steps.text: Double-knot every matching front/back pair, then tie neighbouring ends together to close gaps.
steps.check: No gaps remain for small items to fall through.

steps.title: Turn and test
steps.text: Turn right side out. Add light objects and lift just above the floor.
steps.check: Knots hold and handles do not stretch excessively.

tshirt-tote.limitations: Light-duty use only. Avoid sharp or heavy items and keep away from young children. No rated load.

test.name: Observation
test.instruction: Record the light items used and inspect knots after five lifts.

cereal-gift-bag.title: Reused cereal gift box
cereal-gift-bag.description: Give a small, light gift a new home in reused packaging.

requirements.label: One clean cereal box
requirements.why: Free of grease and food odour.

requirements.label: Two sheets of used paper or magazine pages
Scissors
requirements.why: Choose scissors that can safely cut this material.

steps.title: Check the fit
steps.text: Try the gift in the box first. Choose a sound box whose top can close.
steps.check: The gift does not bulge the sides.

steps.title: Cover the outside
steps.text: Cut paper to cover each side, fold spare edges inward and tape at the corners.
steps.check: The lid folds remain usable.
steps.safety: Ask an adult to help with thick material. Cut away from your hands and keep small scraps away from young children.

steps.title: Add a message and close
steps.text: Write a message on a clear area. Insert the gift, fold the top closed and use only enough tape to keep it shut.
steps.check: The recipient can open it without a blade.

cereal-gift-bag.limitations: For dry, light gifts, not direct food contact.

test.name: Observation
test.instruction: Support the base and lift/set down five times, checking the seams.

woven-coaster.title: Woven paper coaster
woven-coaster.description: Practise weaving with saved paper and make a coaster for dry cups.

requirements.label: Two paper sheets or magazine pages
Scissors
requirements.why: Choose scissors that can safely cut this material.

steps.title: Make paper strips
steps.text: Cut at least ten strips about 4 × 18 cm. Fold each lengthwise into a 1 cm-wide band.
steps.check: The bands have similar widths.

steps.title: Lay the first direction
steps.text: Place five bands side by side. Temporarily tape one end to a surface that the tape will not damage.
steps.check: The bands are parallel.

steps.title: Weave over and under
steps.text: Weave five more bands alternately over and under. Reverse the pattern in the next row and snug them into a square.
steps.check: Each row interlocks with its neighbours.

steps.title: Finish and test
steps.text: Fold spare ends underneath and tape them. Place an empty, dry cup on the coaster.
steps.check: The cup sits flat without rocking.

woven-coaster.limitations: Not waterproof or heat-resistant. Do not use under hot cookware or hot cups; dry or discard if wet.

test.name: Observation
test.instruction: Try two sizes of empty cup and record stability.

bottle-planter.title: Bottle wick planter
bottle-planter.description: Explore how a cotton wick carries water into a small planter.

requirements.label: One 1–1.5 litre plastic bottle with cap
requirements.why: Use a clean food or drink bottle.

requirements.label: About 30 cm of absorbent cotton cord
About 300–500 ml of potting mix
requirements.why: Enough for the bottle top without compacting.

requirements.label: One small seedling
requirements.why: Choose a plant suited to moist, not saturated, mix.

requirements.label: Clean water for the reservoir
requirements.why: Keep the level below the inverted neck.

requirements.label: Hand awl used by an adult
requirements.why: Make a hole in the cap on a stable support; no heating.

requirements.label: Stable scrap-wood backing
requirements.why: Back the cap while keeping hands clear.

requirements.label: Scissors
requirements.why: Choose scissors that can safely cut this material.

requirements.label: Fine insect mesh with openings no larger than 1 mm
requirements.why: Enough to cover every reservoir opening without gaps for mosquitoes.

steps.title: Have an adult prepare the bottle
steps.text: Mark the bottle around its middle. Have an adult make a starter opening and cut it into two parts. Tape the cut edges.
steps.check: The inverted top sits securely in the bottom.
steps.safety: Bottles can slip and cut edges can be sharp. An adult must cut and pierce; never melt holes.

steps.title: Fit the wick
steps.text: Have an adult make a snug cord hole in the cap. Thread cord through with length on both sides, refit the cap and invert the top.
steps.check: The bottom end reaches the reservoir base and the top reaches the root zone.

steps.title: Add mix and a seedling
steps.text: Wet the wick. Add damp mix around it, position the seedling and gently fill around the roots.
steps.check: The mix is not compacted and roots are undamaged.

steps.title: Fill and monitor
steps.text: Fill the reservoir so the wick is immersed but the neck stays above water. Seal every opening with fine insect mesh and tape. Check moisture and the cover daily; refill as needed. Empty and clean the reservoir every 2–3 days and replace the cover.
steps.check: The mix is moist, not saturated, and the mesh is intact with no open gaps. Empty and stop using the reservoir if it cannot be fully covered.

bottle-planter.limitations: Experimental, not a guaranteed unattended watering system. Monitor it; adjust or stop if waterlogged.

test.name: Observation
test.instruction: Record reservoir level and soil moisture at the same time daily; do not infer plant consumption from evaporation alone.

seed-pots.title: Cardboard seed-starting pots
seed-pots.description: Start seeds in cardboard tubes supported by a reused tray.

requirements.label: One tray or food container
requirements.why: Supports pots and catches excess water.

requirements.label: One packet or set of seeds
requirements.why: Follow seed-specific depth and growing conditions.

requirements.label: Water to moisten the mix
requirements.why: Add a little at a time.

requirements.label: Scissors
requirements.why: Choose scissors that can safely cut this material.

steps.title: Fold the bases
steps.text: Cut four roughly 2 cm slits at one end of each tube. Fold the flaps over one another to form a base and stand in the tray.
steps.check: The tubes stand when grouped together.

steps.title: Fill with damp mix
steps.text: Fill with damp, not wet, mix, leaving 1 cm at the top. Label each tube.
steps.check: The mix remains loose.

steps.title: Sow to the packet depth
steps.text: Sow the number and depth specified on the seed packet. Cover as directed.
steps.check: Labels match the seeds.

steps.title: Monitor and transplant
steps.text: Use the light conditions required by the seed. Water gently, empty standing water, and transplant when roots fill the tube.
steps.check: Check daily; isolate and discard mouldy or rotting material.

seed-pots.limitations: Cardboard softens when wet and needs tray support. Do not use mouldy materials.

test.name: Observation
test.instruction: Record sowing date, emergence date and actual germination counts.

propagation-jar.title: Plant propagation observation jar
propagation-jar.description: Watch roots develop in a clear jar and keep a simple observation log.

requirements.label: One water-propagating plant cutting
requirements.why: For example, a pothos cutting with a node supplied by its owner.

requirements.label: Clean water
requirements.why: Enough to cover the node, not the leaves.

steps.title: Select a suitable cutting
steps.text: Use an owner-supplied cutting with at least one node. Check that the species can root in water.
steps.check: You know the species and its handling precautions.
steps.safety: Pothos is toxic if eaten. Keep away from children and pets and wash hands after handling.

steps.title: Submerge a node
steps.text: Fill the jar and position the cutting so a node is under water and all leaves stay above it.
steps.check: No submerged leaves.

steps.title: Use indirect light
steps.text: Place on a stable surface in indirect light, away from edges, harsh sun and electrical equipment.
steps.check: The jar stays cool and cannot spill on equipment.

steps.title: Refresh and record
steps.text: Check daily. Replace cloudy water and refresh regularly; clean any film from the jar. Gently measure roots weekly.
steps.check: Remove rotting cuttings; not every cutting will root.

propagation-jar.limitations: Not all species root in water. Jar water is not drinking water.

test.name: Observation
test.instruction: Record root length in cm weekly, with dates and the plant species.

plant-labels.title: Craft-stick plant labels
plant-labels.description: Keep plant names and sowing dates close to each pot.

steps.title: Choose smooth sticks
steps.text: Wash and dry the sticks. Reject splintered, split or mouldy pieces.
steps.check: Edges are smooth to handle.

steps.title: Write a short label
steps.text: Write the plant name and sowing date on the top half, leaving the lower half blank.
steps.check: Text stays visible above the soil.

steps.title: Place clear of roots
steps.text: Insert gently near the pot edge. If you meet roots, choose another spot.
steps.check: The label neither shades the plant nor damages roots.

plant-labels.limitations: Wood and ink weather when wet. Check and replace labels as needed.

test.name: Observation
test.instruction: Check legibility after a week of normal plant care.

marble-maze.title: Shoebox marble maze
marble-maze.description: Design a route and tilt the box to guide a marble to the finish.

requirements.label: One shoebox or deep box lid
Scissors
requirements.why: Choose scissors that can safely cut this material.

steps.title: Sketch a route
steps.text: Measure the marble diameter. Sketch a route at least 5 mm wider than it.
steps.check: There is a connected route from start to finish.

steps.title: Make the walls
steps.text: Cut about 2 cm-high wall strips and fold small feet along their bottoms for taping.
steps.check: The walls are higher than the marble’s radius.
steps.safety: Ask an adult to help with thick material. Cut away from your hands and keep small scraps away from young children.

steps.title: Attach and check the route
steps.text: Tape walls along the sketch, add the marble and slowly tilt the box by hand.
steps.check: There are no unintended traps.
steps.safety: Marbles are a choking hazard. Keep away from young children and account for the marble afterwards.

steps.title: Adjust difficulty
steps.text: Change one wall position and try five runs. Count successful finishes.
steps.check: Compare under the same route rules.

marble-maze.limitations: For children beyond mouthing age with supervision. Do not throw marbles.

test.name: Observation
test.instruction: Record successful runs out of five before and after a wall change.

moving-hand.title: String-powered cardboard hand
moving-hand.description: Explore a tendon-like mechanism with cardboard, straws and string.

requirements.label: Scissors
requirements.why: Choose scissors that can safely cut this material.

steps.title: Trace and cut a hand
steps.text: Trace a hand with enough space between fingers to cut, then cut out the hand and a short wrist.
steps.check: Every finger stays attached to the palm.
steps.safety: Ask an adult to help with thick material. Cut away from your hands and keep small scraps away from young children.

steps.title: Mark the joints
steps.text: Mark two or three joints per finger and gently fold toward the palm.
steps.check: Each joint bends freely.

steps.title: Add straw guides
steps.text: Cut straws into short pieces. Tape a guide on each finger segment, leaving every joint clear.
steps.check: No straw bridges a folding joint.

steps.title: Thread and pull
steps.text: Tape a cord end at each fingertip on the palm side. Thread it through the guides toward the wrist. Gently pull one cord at a time.
steps.check: A pull bends the finger; straighten it manually when released.

moving-hand.limitations: A model, not a prosthesis or automatic robot. Do not wrap cords around the body.

test.name: Observation
test.instruction: Try five pulls per finger and record sticking points and adjustments.

paper-bridge.title: Folded paper bridge experiment
paper-bridge.description: Compare flat and folded paper using the same material and span.

requirements.label: Two equal-size paper sheets
requirements.why: Use the same paper type and thickness.

requirements.label: Two food containers of equal height

steps.title: Set the span
steps.text: Place supports on a low table with about a 10 cm gap. Measure it and keep it unchanged.
steps.check: Supports are level and stable.

steps.title: Test a flat sheet
steps.text: Lay a sheet across with equal overlap at both ends. Add coins one at a time at the centre; stop at collapse.
steps.check: Record the number before collapse without supporting by hand.

steps.title: Fold an accordion
steps.text: Accordion-fold the second sheet into roughly 2 cm panels. Place the ridges along the span, crossing the gap.
steps.check: Keep the same span and loading position.

steps.title: Compare and explain
steps.text: Repeat the loading. If it holds all ten coins, record at least ten; do not guess the maximum.
steps.check: Compare observed results and state the available coin limit.
steps.safety: Keep coins away from young children. Test low down; never support a person.

paper-bridge.limitations: An educational model. Results depend on paper and span; not a construction design.

test.name: Observation
test.instruction: Record span, coin count before collapse, and fold pattern for each design.
